# GEMM performance — sm_100 / sm_103 (NVIDIA B300)

<!-- The tables are generated by bench/gemm/python/render_perf_docs.py from tests/baselines/*.jsonl; do not edit them by hand. -->

Each row is one GEMM at one M, or in the grouped tables one grouped MoE GEMM over the experts of one projection, timed
alone in a CUDA graph with cold weights: the graph rotates through R copies of the weight, with R × weight bytes ≥ 2 ×
L2, and reports the replay time divided by R. BF16 is the unquantized reference, `torch.nn.functional.linear` on
cuBLAS; BSFP8 (block-scaled FP8) and MXFP8 are fso's GEMMs, each reported as µs per call, TFLOPS and `cos`, the cosine
similarity of its output against the BF16 output. In the grouped tables `m_cap` is the row capacity of each expert and
`weight GB/s` the rate at which the kernel reads the weights of the active experts. The B300 runs at its natural
clock, without a lock, while a clock sampler records the clock. The method is in [`../README.md`](../README.md), and
the run that produced each baseline file is named in its [Environments of record](../README.md#environments-of-record)
block. Whole-layer numbers and the comparisons against other libraries are in
[`../layer/sm100.md`](../layer/sm100.md).

On this arch BSFP8 runs the same GEMM as MXFP8 after expanding its scales, so a gap between the two FP8 columns is
measurement scatter, not a format difference. The dense prefill rows (large M) run under the board power cap, so they
scatter more between runs. The tables were measured with the optional `nvidia-cutlass-dsl` package installed
([`../../guide.md`](../../guide.md) §2); without it some shapes run on slower paths.
